findings.obs_text: In Act 26:8 raising the dead is what is thought incredible: the thought judges God's act unbelievable. In 2Cor 10:5 the proud reasonings set up against knowing God are torn down and every thought is made captive: the raising is of pride against God, and the thought is brought under Christ.
findings.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

findings.obs_text: In Pro 15:26 the Lord abhors the thoughts of the wicked: the thoughts themselves are judged by him. In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future, and her fall is terrible: the lack of thought is followed by the fall.
findings.grounds: The thoughts of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord

findings.obs_text: In Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 evil thoughts come first in the list of what comes out of the heart, before murder, adultery and the others: the thoughts are the first of the evils that issue from the heart.
findings.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

older.finding: moicheia (G3430, noun) as a vice-list item, listed among evil thoughts, theft and murder from the heart (Mark 7:21, Matt 15:19): the abstract-state noun naming a category of heart-originating evil rather than a specific incident.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the adultery words; the adultery collection owns it

older.finding: Adultery in and from the heart: "committed adultery with her in his heart" (Mat 5:28); "out of the heart come … adultery" (Mat 15:19; Mar 7:21); "He who commits adultery lacks sense [*heart*]; he who does it destroys himself [*his nephesh*]" (Pro 6:32) — cf. Batch C §1.5; "eyes full of adultery … They entice unsteady souls. They have hearts trained in greed" (2Pe 2:14)
older.reason: it states how adultery works in a person; the adultery collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 40:5 the Lord's wondrous deeds and his thoughts toward his people are named together as many: his thoughts stand with his works.
findings.grounds: your wondrous deeds and your thoughts toward us

findings.obs_text: In 2Ki 5:11 Naaman is angry and goes away saying what he had thought Elisha would do: his anger rises from the thought that was not met.
findings.grounds: But Naaman was angry and went away

older.finding: 2Ki 5:11-14: Naaman "was angry and went away ... turned and went away in a rage"; his inner thought is quoted ("Behold, I thought that he would surely come out"); the servants talk him round (5:13), and "his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child" (5:14): rage, persuasion, obedience, restoration, with no seat word anywhere.
older.reason: it states how anger works in a person; the anger collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Luk 5:22 Jesus perceives their thoughts and asks why they question in their hearts: the thoughts are the questioning within. In Eph 3:20 asking and thinking are joined as what God can do beyond.
findings.grounds: Why do you question in your hearts

older.finding: Questioning in the heart, perceived in the spirit: "some of the scribes … questioning in their hearts … Jesus, perceiving in his spirit" (Mar 2:6–8) [H]; "Why do you question in your hearts?" (Luk 5:22); "all were questioning in their hearts concerning John" (Luk 3:15).
older.reason: it states how ask works in a person; the ask collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In 2Cor 11:3 Paul fears the thoughts will be led astray from sincere devotion to Christ, as the serpent deceived Eve: the thoughts are what deceit leads off. In Mat 18:12 astray is the sheep of the parable, asked about with what do you think.
findings.grounds: your thoughts will be led astray

findings.obs_text: In Judg 15:2 the father says he thought Samson hated her and offers the younger, more beautiful sister: the mistaken thought led to the giving, and beauty is his offer in its place.
findings.grounds: Is not her younger sister more beautiful than she
